nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: The entire FixUp Arena marketing/landing page — a single static HTML file combining Tailwind-styled markup for four faux 'views' (home, privacy, terms, support), a Three.js particle background, GSAP/ScrollTrigger scroll animations, and vanilla JS hash-based client-side navigation, with Stripe Payment Links for registration.
nodes.languageNotes: All HTML, CSS, and JavaScript live in one file with no bundler; dependencies (Tailwind, Three.js, GSAP, ScrollTrigger, Iconify, fonts) are loaded from CDNs directly in <head>. JS uses history.pushState/popstate plus location.hash to fake multi-page routing within a single DOM.

nodes.name: navigateTo
nodes.summary: Toggles page-visible/page-hidden classes on the four view containers (#home-view, #privacy-view, #tos-view, #support-view) to fake page navigation, updates browser history state and the URL hash, and re-runs ScrollTrigger.refresh() so scroll animations recalibrate for the newly shown view.

nodes.name: openMenu
nodes.summary: Opens the mobile navigation menu overlay, wired to the menu button's click handler.

nodes.name: closeMenu
nodes.summary: Closes the mobile navigation menu overlay, wired to the close button's click handler.

nodes.name: tick
nodes.summary: Per-frame render loop callback that animates and redraws the Three.js particle scene (stadium crowd and helix) behind the page content.

tour.title: Project Guidance & Architecture Overview
tour.description: Start with CLAUDE.md, the project's guidance document for AI assistants. It explains that FixUp Arena is a single static index.html landing page with no build step at all — no bundler, no framework, no package.json — and previews the three moving parts you'll explore next: hash-based view switching, a Three.js particle background, and GSAP/ScrollTrigger scroll animations.

tour.title: The Entire Site: index.html
tour.description: index.html is the whole application — every view, style, and script lives in this one file. It combines Tailwind-styled markup for four faux 'views' (home, privacy, terms, support), a Three.js particle background, GSAP/ScrollTrigger scroll animations, and vanilla JS hash-based navigation, with Stripe Payment Links handling registration. Because there's no build tooling, what you read here is exactly what ships to the browser.
tour.languageLesson: Single-file static sites trade modularity for zero build complexity: HTML, CSS (via Tailwind's CDN/utility classes), and JS all live together, so the entire page can be understood by scrolling one file top to bottom.

tour.title: Faking Multiple Pages: navigateTo
tour.description: Since there's no server-side routing or framework router, navigateTo() is what makes this feel like a multi-page site. It reads the URL hash and toggles which 'view' section (home, privacy, terms, support) is visible, giving the illusion of separate pages while staying a single HTML document. This is the core navigation mechanism tying together everything else in the file.
tour.languageLesson: Hash-based routing (#privacy, #terms) works without any server configuration because the hash never triggers a page reload — JavaScript just listens for hashchange and swaps visible DOM sections.

tour.title: Mobile Navigation: openMenu / closeMenu
tour.description: openMenu() and closeMenu() control the mobile hamburger navigation, a small but essential piece of UX alongside navigateTo(). Together these three functions form the site's complete interaction layer — everything a visitor clicks to move around the page.

tour.title: The Animated Background: tick
tour.description: tick() is the render loop driving the Three.js particle background — the animated visual backdrop behind the marketing content. It's called continuously (typically via requestAnimationFrame) to update particle positions and redraw the scene each frame, running independently of the navigation logic covered in the previous steps.
tour.languageLesson: A 'tick' function is the standard name for a render-loop callback in real-time graphics: each call advances animation state by one frame, and the loop re-invokes itself (via requestAnimationFrame) for smooth 60fps rendering without blocking the main thread.
